Messages.Author: Rawlings family
Messages.Body:
As promised, really quickly thrown together and not tested, but this is
about the worst case of Rotschreck abuse that I could think of. The
question is, is it, after some tweaking, worthy enough to win tournaments
with?

Thoughts? Oh, and if anyone thinks they have a worse Rotschreck deck
concept, feel free to share.

Deck Name: Broken!
Created By: Derek Rawlings
Description: Intercept your prey (with Eagle's Sight if necessary), use
Rötschreck to cut down them down, then use deadly bleeds to off him. Grave
rob with impunity. Repeat as needed.

Messages.Author: Thomas Pichler
Messages.Body:
Rawlings family wrote:
>
> As promised, really quickly thrown together and not tested, but this is
> about the worst case of Rotschreck abuse that I could think of. The
> question is, is it, after some tweaking, worthy enough to win
> tournaments with?
>
> Thoughts? Oh, and if anyone thinks they have a worse Rotschreck deck
> concept, feel free to share.
>

You're not going to kill a S&B prey. Not enough intercept to block +2
stealth forward D actions more than two or three times a game, and no
real combat ability when you're actiong.
I'm not sure it could actually kill a prey if having to defend against
any predator but S&B. Doubt it.

A deck with fewer Rötschrecks and more of a plan what else it does
should be better 9 times out of 10, I figure.

Thomas

Messages.Author: Derek Ray
Messages.Body:
In message <PVDI9.27953$77.25...@news2.telusplanet.net>,
"Rawlings family" <raw...@telus.net> mumbled something about:

>As promised, really quickly thrown together and not tested, but this is
>about the worst case of Rotschreck abuse that I could think of. The
>question is, is it, after some tweaking, worthy enough to win tournaments
>with?

Not really. Inherent flaws with Rotschreck (that the anti-Rotschreck
people don't think of when they post the rants) cut this one off at the
knees. It's nasty, I'm sure, but ...

>Created By: Derek Rawlings
>Description: Intercept your prey (with Eagle's Sight if necessary), use
>Rötschreck to cut down them down, then use deadly bleeds to off him. Grave
>rob with impunity. Repeat as needed.
>
>Crypt: (12 cards, Min: 17, Max: 32, Avg: 5.92)
>----------------------------------------------

Going with a group 2-3 combo here will give you more AUS/THA.

>1 Hannigan AUS dom THA 5, Tremere Antitribu

2 copies of this guy.

>1 Merrill Molitor aus dom THA 5, Tremere

Sack him for Cohn Rose (for group 3 compatibility); same disciplines,
but no special.

>1 Aisling Sturbridge AUS dom THA 5, Tremere

And 2 copies of her.

>1 Justine AUS DOM obf THA 8, Tremere, Primogen

Take her out to make room for a Hannigan.

>1 Muaziz aus dom for THA 7, Tremere
>1 Richard Tauber AUS tha 4, Tremere Antitribu
>1 Blythe Candeleria aus THA 3, Tremere
>1 Kij Dansky AUS DOM obt THA 8, Tremere Antitribu, Priscus
>2 Reverend Blackwood DOM obf THA 6, Tremere Antitribu, Bishop

This is your worst vamp, with no AUS and a special that is irrelevant
since the damage never happens. Throw him out for 2 copies of Carna,
easily your best vamp for a deck like this.

>1 Kurt Strauss aus DOM tha 5, Tremere Antitribu
>1 Lazarus AUS cel DOM pot THA 9, Tremere, Primogen

And replace this vamp with the other Aisling.

>Library: (90 cards)
>-------------------
>Master (18 cards)
>2 Blood Doll
>1 Millicent Smith, Puritan Vampire Hunter
>15 Rotschreck

Parthenon, Barrens, 2 Suddens, and 3 less Rotschrecks.

>Action (18 cards)
>4 Govern the Unaligned
>10 Graverobbing

First problem. Consider the timing of everything; you intercept your
prey and then he rescues the vamp from torpor immediately, leaving you
no opportunity to Grave Rob the poor guy. Second problem; you have no
stealth on your Grave Robbing, so it won't succeed.

I'd cut this down to 4-6. After the first time you Grave Rob your prey,
the rest of the table will rescue his vamps for him (making him pay the
cost) just so you don't sweep with someone else's vamps.

>2 Pulse of the Canaille
>2 Rutor's Hand
>
>Action Modifier (6 cards)
>3 Conditioning
>3 Foreshadowing Destruction

(shrug) Look, bleed cards!

Since I just peed all over the superior DOM vampires up above, I suggest
using all Conditionings here. The ones you have left will likely be
remaining untapped (only 4 Wakes?!), so you won't be able to use Carna
to chuck around a bleed of 4.

>Reaction (27 cards)
>5 Deflection
>8 Eagle's Sight
>2 Enhanced Senses
>2 My Enemy's Enemy
>2 Precognition
>2 Spirit's Touch
>2 Telepathic Misdirection
>4 Wake with Evening's Freshness

You're intercept light here, meaning you REALLY need Carna. Since you
have spare slots from above, I would add two more Eagle's Sight, two
more Enhanced Senses, replace both Precognition with Spirit's Touch, and
replace both Telepathic Misdirection with Spirit's Touch. You have to
maneuver; if you are Grappled, you can't Rotschreck.

This is going to be a problem for you anyway, because POT decks won't
let you play Spirit's Touch, but there's one primary weakness right now.

You are also Wake-light, which is worrisome. You should certainly swap
the first 4 Wakes for Forced Awakening (since you're an intercept deck,
you can expect to block), and maybe swap some of the Deflections for
Forced Awakening as well (you ARE an intercept deck).

>Combat (19 cards)
>15 Burst of Sunlight
>4 Theft of Vitae

You have no defense for after you've played your first Rotschreck. This
will cause immediate, tragic difficulty. The extra maneuvers I just
gave you with Spirit's Touch will work well, but I suggest dropping down
to 12 Burst and up to 8 Theft.

>Retainer (1 cards)
>1 Mr. Winthrop
>
>Equipment (1 cards)
>1 Sport Bike

Anyone worth their salt won't let you get either of these. Toss Mr.
Winthrop; he's contestable and free. The Sport Bike, oddly enough,
might be something your predator lets you have because of the 1 pool
cost; and if you DO get it, you don't have to worry about someone
contesting it away from you later (or Far Masterying it).

Could someone win with this? Anything's possible. Is it enough to show
Rotschreck as broken? No. If anything, it paints up the weaknesses in
a big old limelight.

--
"There's no gray. There's just white that's got grubby." -- T.P.

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
Rawlings family wrote:

> As promised, really quickly thrown together and not tested, but this is
> about the worst case of Rotschreck abuse that I could think of. The
> question is, is it, after some tweaking, worthy enough to win tournaments
> with?

I doubt it. It certainly looks pretty funny, and possibly even effective,
but it has incredibly limited pool gain and it's ability to reliably
torporize minions is limited to one per turn around the table, it doesn't
have enough intercept (or untap) to realiably stop even moderate stealth,
and it has limited forward momentum (6 bleed increase cards?). This deck
will be really good at sending one minion to torpor once around the table,
while getting savaged by bleeds or combat--what does this deck do against
rush? It has no manuvers, it can't play Burst if Immortally Grappled. It has
limited defense against heavy bleeds (5 Deflections and middling intercept).
All in all, a possibly sometimes useful deck. I hardly see it dominating a
tournament, let alone even winning much.

How is this going to be any more effective than:

A) a standard IG Rush deck (which can torporize 3-4 minions a turn).

B) a standard Tremere intercept/burn deck (which can generally torporized
more than 1 minion a turn).

Peter D Bakija

Messages.Author: Rawlings family
Messages.Body:
I made this deck more as an example than anything else. Someone made the
assertion that Rotschreck was broken, other people said it's not. This deck
was intended (after some tweaking) to be the worst possible Rotschreck deck
you could make.

It was really to prove that even with the most vile Rotschreck creation you
could make, it's still not going to be any more broken then say a rush deck,
which can be many times more efficient (torp 2 or more vamps in a turn).

Anyways, I think my point is proven.

Derek

Rotschreck, yet still isn't all that hot, the deck in question is a pretty
good example. Again, the deck certainly looks entertaining, and might even
do ok, but has huge gaping holes (if it sits next to an IG rush deck, it is
complete meat. If it sits next to a standard S+B deck, it is complete meat.
If it sits next to a weenie Pre deck, it is complete meat...)

>

I'm sure there is a more effective Rotschreck deck out there. And even then,
it isn't going to be that handy :-)

> Library: (90 cards)
> -------------------

> 1 Millicent Smith, Puritan Vampire Hunter
> 15 Rotschreck

This is a bit excessive. I bet you could get similar results with 8-10
Rotschreck, which would still qualify as a Rotschreck deck IMO. Add
some more blood management in place of the Rots. Also one Auspex
master to be sure (for Muaziz). Perhaps an intercept location or two.
Wassershloss Anif is also fun for this sort of deck.

> Action (18 cards)
> 4 Govern the Unaligned
> 10 Graverobbing
> 2 Pulse of the Canaille
> 2 Rutor's Hand

More Governs, less Graverobs. You don't need the Dom modifiers if
you've already taken your prey's minions into torpor. Plus, with the
bigger voting vampires, bloating can help tremendously. 1-2 Magic of
the Smith might be nice and perhaps Far Mastery. Probably want a
couple Nose of the Hound so you can bring the combat when necessary.

> Action Modifier (6 cards)
> 3 Conditioning
> 3 Foreshadowing Destruction
>
> Reaction (27 cards)
> 5 Deflection
> 8 Eagle's Sight
> 2 Enhanced Senses
> 2 My Enemy's Enemy
> 2 Precognition
> 2 Spirit's Touch
> 2 Telepathic Misdirection
> 4 Wake with Evening's Freshness
>
> Combat (19 cards)
> 15 Burst of Sunlight
> 4 Theft of Vitae

Too much intercept, not enough standard combat. You've made a "trick"
deck which isn't going to win all that much, but a HEALTHY does of
Rotschreck can really boost the power of Tremere intercept.
Apportations, and Walk of Flames are all good here. Could even get
fancy with Shotguns and Amaranths. I'd pull 3-5 Reactions and 7-8
Bursts. You won't need as much bounce because you want to fight. Only
a supremely heavy stealth deck will get past you. If you pack enough
permanent intercept you won't have to worry much.

> Equipment (1 cards)
> 1 Sport Bike

You're missing the ever critical Ivory Bow in this deck. :) A Rowan
Ring and/or Sengir Dagger might not be out of place either.

I'll have to see how many Rotshrecks I have (I think only 4 or 5)
before putting this monster together. Time to inspire some table hate.
;)

Succubus Club [Jyhad, V:TES, CE]
Cardtype: Master
Master: unique location.
During your untap phase, you may tap this card to trade with a Methuselah who
agrees to trade. You may trade pool and cards from your hand and cards you
control. The trade cannot result in either Methuselah have fewer cards in hand
than his or her hand size. Any additional terms can be established, but none
are enforced by the rules.

Eye of Hazimel
Type(s): Equipment
Pool Cost: 3
Artist(s): Kieran Yanner
Set(s): *Promotional
Unique Equipment
The minion with this equipment gets +1 bleed and +1 strength. This minion may
enter combat with any minion controlled by another Methuselah as a (D) action.
If this minion is a vampire, he or she has superior Chimerstry and superior
Potence, and combat cards cost this vampire one less blood to play. While the
bearer is ready, this equipment cannot be transferred, moved or stolen. If this
equipment is burned, this minion takes 5 unpreventable damage. During your
